scope: shape boundaries, solidity, facial scale, and runtime hierarchy; existing Suma palette, species data, animation, and lighting remain authoritative
observations: The current non-human renderer smooth-unions torso, head, muzzle, limbs, feet, wings, tail, and ears into one SDF surface.
Unrelated parts visibly melt together at their contacts and their colors cross-fade through the shared distance field.
Overlapping seed charts create doubled contour and interior-looking artifacts that make some creatures read as hollow or translucent.
The generic muzzle patch and owl face discs occupy most of the face, producing mask-like expressions.
The generic and owl eye shapes are tall and large relative to the head, increasing the uncanny expression.
inferences: Species-specific rear and side silhouettes remain driven by their existing JSON definitions because the supplied reference is a single gameplay view.
The complaint about opacity is treated as a solidity and surface-ownership problem rather than a request for transparent materials.

componentRules.surface: one bounded closed procedural mesh, never fused with torso
independent closed tapered mesh when authored
one closed native tapered-capsule mesh per source segment, grouped under the Legs semantic node
one closed native sphere mesh per foot, grouped under the Feet semantic node
one closed native tapered-capsule mesh per arm, grouped under the Arms semantic node
one closed native sphere mesh per hand, grouped under the Hands semantic node
one closed native tapered-capsule mesh per wing segment, grouped under the Wings semantic node
one closed native tapered-capsule mesh per tail segment
one closed native tapered-capsule mesh per ear, grouped under the Ears semantic node
independent matte graphic geometry parented to the head frame
independent matte graphic geometry parented to the torso frame

materialRules: Every semantic mesh is closed, opaque, and uses its explicitly assigned palette color.
No distance-color interpolation may cross semantic-part boundaries.
Non-touching peers share only a semantic parent and material; they retain independent closed geometry.
Coat patterns may be evaluated on every body shell, but gloss remains bounded by the existing shader's rough painted-surface response.
Face and belly graphics remain unshaded, matte, and independent from the body distance field.
acceptance: CreatureSdfShell remains only as a hidden compatibility node for every non-human creature.
Every visible non-human creature has a CreatureParts native procedural-mesh hierarchy.
No visible semantic surface contains shapes from two unrelated body parts.
Every source shape is assigned exactly once and the assigned total equals shape_budget().
All creature definitions build and animate without changing their JSON schema.
Front and three-quarter menagerie captures read as solid characters with distinct head, body, limbs, and face graphics.
